items.t: Muḥammad and to the family of our master Muḥammad, and to fulfil my need entire: what I ask for and what I do not ask for, of that wherein You have good pleasure, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. And this is the end of what has been set down of the faṣl. And God, glorified and exalted, knows best.
Chapter 7 (al-bāb al-sābiʿ): On the names by which our master Jesus — peace be upon him — used to bring the dead to life, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted [83]

Know — may God grant me and you success in obedience to Him — that these names are of mighty import. The Imām al-Khwārizmī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said: I sought the Greatest Name for seven years, and I found it with none but a man of the people of China. He had gathered together of these names a mighty matter, and I found them written in his keeping in the Ḥimyarī script, so that none should know them save their [rightful] people.

And ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said: Whoever fasts for them seven days, then, when the seventh day comes, let him write these names upon gazelle parchment with musk, saffron, and rose water; then let him invoke by the names of the angels of the seasonal quarter (thāqūfa) in which that operation is performed — the thāqūfa being the quarter of the year — and let him adjure by the names of the winds, according as Abraham, the Friend of the All-Merciful — peace be upon him — named them. Then after that you mention your need and ask for it. And if it be possible for that to be over running water, it is better. And you hang it up toward the sun and mention what you desire, and you recite over it the names of the angels of the thāqūfa and its helpers, and the winds and the planets that belong to it.

Al-Khwārizmī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said: When he met with the Chinese master mentioned above, when he asked him about the Greatest Name, he said: O my son, know that every name of the names of God, exalted is He, is mighty. I said: Yes, but I have already come to know many of them. Then the master questioned me about the thāqūfa of Balʿām b. Bāʿūrā and the thāqūfa of Joseph, and I informed him of them both; for the master had supposed that I had not gained access to the treasured names. Thereupon the master said: Draw near to me — by God, no comer has come to me dearer than you. I said: Yes. So I drew near to him, and we did not cease conferring together /fol. 43v./ concerning the names. Then I asked him about the names that were upon the staff of Moses — peace be upon him — but he did not know them. Al-Khwārizmī said: And he it was who dictated to me the Greatest Name. He said to me: O my son, know that the most exalted of the names of God, exalted is He, and the greatest of them, are these names, if God, exalted is He, wills. And these ancient names were written in a foreign tongue, and some of them in Hebrew, so that none should know them. And they are the majestic names. And their excellence and their blessing is what Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — related from Ḥumayd b. Abī Thābit from Abū Khālid — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — who said: I heard a man of the people of knowledge say: The excellence of these names over all [other] names is like the excellence of the Night of Power over all other nights, and like the excellence of Friday over all other days.

The Imām al-Khwārizmī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said: I found them written in the Ḥimyarī script in a place called Qazwīn. So whoever understands their excellence, it is incumbent upon him that he guard them well, and then that he fear God, mighty and exalted. And they are beneficial for one afflicted with anguish or with terror, or for one who has trembling, or griping [of the bowels], or palpitation of the heart. And Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: If one fasts for them three days, then writes them upon a clean, white gazelle parchment with saffron, then hangs it upon one afflicted with the wind, or with the evil eye (naẓra), or with black bile, or with something other than that — it departs from him in the swiftest time that may be. And it is said, in [another] transmission: you write them on Saturday for whatever you desire; you fast that day of yours, and you write them upon gazelle parchment after you have ascertained the house of the Moon — whether it be the best of the good, or the contrary of that. And it is said that Jesus — upon whom be blessing and peace — used to bring the dead to life by them, and to heal by it the man born blind and the leper, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And they are written in the lowest heaven. They are to be written on Friday. The people of knowledge have agreed upon their interpretation, and it is that upon which the Commander of the Faithful al-Maʾmūn gathered the jurists, the scholars, and the sages, until, in his presence, their interpretation was verified. And whoever is assiduous in the mention of them and is in accord with God, exalted is He — God, exalted is He, rends for him the customary order of things, and the objects of desire and the benefits come within his reach. So beware of treating them with contempt; make them the greatest of your concern; hold fast to them all your life long; make them your stored treasure; and make them your litany (wird) by day and by night — you will win the station of sainthood (wilāya), and attain the ranks of the God-fearing.

And from Abū l-Hudhayl — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — who said: When Jesus — upon whom be blessing and peace — desired to bring the dead to life, he would pray two rakʿas, reciting in the first the Mother of the Book (the Fātiḥa) and Alif-Lām-Mīm al-Sajda, and in the second the Mother of the Book and Blessed is He in whose hand is the kingdom, and He is powerful over everything (Q 67:1). Then, when he had finished his prayer, he would prostrate himself before God, mighty and exalted, and praise Him. Then he would invoke by the seven names whose invocation is answered, and these are the names: /fol. 44r./ O Qadīm (Eternal), O Ḥayy (Living), O Dāʾim (Everlasting), O Fard (Single), O Aḥad (Unique), O Wāḥid (One), O Ṣamad (Eternal Refuge). Muqātil b. Sulaymān — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: I kept seeking the names by which our master Jesus — peace be upon him — used to bring the dead to life, for forty years, until I found them with a man of the people of knowledge and religion; and they are these names mentioned above. And Muqātil b. Sulaymān — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: Whoever invokes by them after the dawn prayer one hundred times and asks for whatever need he desires — if he is not answered, then let him curse Muqātil, be he alive or dead. And they may also be invoked for the destruction of the wrongdoers and of the tyrants, and for other things besides that. So when you have prayed the dawn prayer, say, while seated, before you speak with anyone, one hundred times: "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. O Qadīm (Eternal), O Qāʾim (Subsisting), O Dāʾim (Everlasting), O Fard (Single), O Witr (Odd-numbered), O Aḥad (Unique), O Ṣamad (Eternal Refuge), O Ḥayy (Living), O Qayyūm (Self-Subsisting), O Karīm (Generous), O Raḥīm (Compassionate), O Sanad (Support), O You unto whom is all reliance, O You who did not beget and were not begotten, and to whom none is equal (Q 112:3–4), O Possessor of Majesty and Honour." Then, when you have completed the hundred times, ask for your need, whatever it may be. And if you are not answered, then curse Muqātil, be he alive or dead. And as for these names: when you invoke by them, beware of invoking by them against anyone, lest the invocation turn back upon you. And if you invoke and ask, then ask for what befits you of the affair of your livelihood, in a matter of this world or of religion, or the teaching of knowledge from which benefit is had, and the like of that — for they are mighty, noble, majestic names.

And when you desire the operative deployment (taṣrīf) of the Greatest Name, then make a circle like the circle of the sun, the names being within it, and suffumigate it with aloeswood and ambergris and the like of that. And this is the form of the circle, as you see.

And this is the invocation of the Greatest Name. You say: O God, I ask You by that whereby Gabriel — peace be upon him — asked You when he prostrated himself beside Your mighty Throne, and by the right of Your name Allāh Allāh, that You subject to me Your angels, and the servitors of Your Throne and the Presence of Your dominion: Kasfiyāʾīl, and

Dardiyāʾīl, and Samḥiyāʾīl, and Samʿiyāʾīl, and Rūqiyāʾīl, and Nūriyāʾīl, and Samkiyāʾīl, and Ṭahṭahāʾīl, and Jibriyāʾīl, and Darʿiyāʾīl, and Samsamāʾīl, and Ṭāṭāʾīl, and Ḥarmiyāʾīl, and Ṭayṭiyāʾīl, and Isrāfīl, and ʿAzrāʾīl, and Mīkāʾīl, and Karmāʾih, and Karshāʾih, and Sarfiyāʾīl, and ʿArqiyāʾīl, and Thaṭbiyāʾīl, and ʿAyniyāʾīl. Answer me, by the noble angels and the good spirits — peace be upon them — who are brought near to God by [the affirmation of] His oneness; by the right of the name of God, the One, the Magnified, the Light most holy, which You have preferred above all the names entirely — the mighty of them and the impregnable of them, the majestic of them and the great of them — [I ask nothing] save that You subject to me these noble angels, that they may fulfil my need, which is such-and-such, and which is a thing wherein God, mighty and exalted, has good pleasure. And beware of what is not lawful; for Balʿām b. Bāʿūrā had good command of the Greatest Name, and when he invoked by it against the people of Moses — upon whom be blessing and peace — the invocation was turned back upon him, and God, exalted is He, stripped him of the Greatest Name. And refuge is with God, exalted is He, from that. And God, exalted is He, has said: And recite to them the tiding of him to whom We brought Our signs, and he stripped himself out of them, whereupon Satan pursued him and he became one of the errant. And had We so willed, We would have lifted him up by them; but he sank down toward the earth and followed his own whim. His likeness, then, is the likeness of the dog: if you drive at it, it pants; and if you leave it be, it pants. That is the likeness of the folk who denied Our signs. So narrate the accounts, that they may perhaps take thought (Q 7:175–176). God, God, concerning this Greatest Name! And beware of making light of it, for it turns back upon you and upon whoever deploys it in acts of disobedience to God, exalted is He. Guard it from those who are not its [rightful] people, and preserve it, and you will be happy; for it is God's secret [entrusted] to His friends and to His elect. Many of the scholars and the righteous have busied themselves with it and have attained by it their desire and their object of search. And we have abridged the discourse; and God guides whom He wills to a straight path. And know — may God grant me and you success in the understanding of His noble names — that whoever writes this treasured, hidden, noble, blessed wafq and carries it, being pure in garment and in body, God, exalted is He, establishes his affair outwardly and inwardly, aids him unto obedience, and provides him with strength and with victory over his enemies. No tyrant's glance falls upon him but he holds him in awe and magnifies him. And whoever places it upon his head, every obstinate tyrant and rebellious satan is abased before him; and God, exalted is He, gives life to his outward and his inward, and strengthens his heart for the outward works and the inward. And no one has carried it and contended with his enemy but that he overcame him, subdued him, and gained the victory over him, by the blessing of God, exalted is He, and the blessing of this blessed wafq. And whoever enters into war having it with him is granted victory over his enemies, and no harm ever reaches him, by the leave of God, exalted is He.
